messages:
alex: Hey folks, hitting a weird combo on Fedora 38 — installing redwoodctl from our dnf repo fails GPG check; I force-installed for testing, then redwoodctl local-serve had a port collision and redwoodctl login got stuck in a retry loop (never sees the OAuth callback). Anyone seen this?

mira: Which version and can you paste the errors/logs?

alex: v0.9.2

alex: dnf error i pasted:
```
Updating Subscription Management repositories.
Error: GPG check FAILED: public key not found
```
I used --nogpgcheck to proceed (not ideal). Then `redwoodctl local-serve` output: 
```
Started local server on 127.0.0.1:49512
Opening browser for login...
Waiting for OAuth callback...
login retry: timeout waiting for callback (retrying)
```

sam: Two quick checks: 1) Confirm the repo file has the correct `gpgkey=` URL (we should avoid --nogpgcheck). 2) Port issue: `ss -ltnp | grep 49512` to see who holds it. Also try `REDWOODCTL_LOCAL_SERVE_PORT=0 redwoodctl local-serve` to let the CLI pick a free port.

alex: ss shows a leftover process holding 49512 (gnome-related). Killed it. Still seeing retries. With `REDWOODCTL_LOCAL_SERVE_PORT=0` the CLI picked port 49513 and printed `Listening on [::]:49513` but the browser callback goes to 127.0.0.1 and the CLI never registers it.

jen: That looks like an IPv4/IPv6 mismatch — CLI bound to both but callback hit IPv4 loopback. Try forcing the listen address: `redwoodctl login --listen-addr 127.0.0.1:49513`. If the CLI doesn't support that flag we should add it. Also run `redwoodctl config list` to check for profile collisions — sometimes an existing `localtest`/`default` profile causes silent failures when login tries to create/overwrite a profile.

alex: Tried `--listen-addr 127.0.0.1:49513` and the callback completed! Login finished.

mira: Good. I'll file two follow-ups: 1) Fedora repo docs to fix the GPG key instructions (avoid suggesting --nogpgcheck) and 2) CLI doc + issue to document `REDWOODCTL_LOCAL_SERVE_PORT` and add a `--listen-addr` flag.

ci-bot: Related doc + issue links: https://docs.redwood.ai/cli/install#fedora-repo  |  https://go/repo/issue/1234

alex: I'll open a tiny PR to docs with the example (explicit --listen-addr and IPv4 note). Thanks :thumbsup:
